meta.title: AI English Coach Dashboard
meta.dataPolicy: 실제 완료 세션만 포함하며 샘플 데이터는 제외합니다.
meta.savePolicy: 음성 인식 여부와 관계없이 텍스트 '세션 저장' 명령을 동일한 GitHub 저장 절차로 처리합니다.
meta.lessonNotePolicy: 완료된 각 세션에는 실제 발화, 핵심 교정, 목표 표현, 최종 버전, 복습 질문과 D+1·D+3·D+7 일정이 포함된 lessonNote를 저장합니다.

sessions.topic: 일정 검토 및 다음 안건 전환
newExpressions: Let's look at the timeline in detail.
sessions.bestSentence: Let's look at the timeline in detail.
sessions.correctedSentence: Let's review the timeline in detail before we move on to the next item.
sessions.feedback: 문장 확장이 안정적. 전치사와 관사 정확도를 집중 보완.

sessions.bestSentence: I will contact local partners to clarify costs of materials.
sessions.correctedSentence: The consultant asked whether we would participate or cooperate.
sessions.feedback: Improved logical flow; work on precise verb forms.
sessions.nextChallenge: Explaining a project delay and requesting a decision.

newExpressions: What is the city known for?
Does the city have any local specialties?
sessions.bestSentence: How was your trip and how was the city?
sessions.correctedSentence: I compared several Logitech models and chose a newer, more affordable one because it offered the features I needed.
sessions.feedback: You sustained an unfamiliar everyday topic and extended your answers with comparisons, reasons, and future possibilities. Frequent sentence restarts and clause-linking errors—especially although...but, tense consistency, relative clauses, and question formation—reduced accuracy. Your speech remained intelligible, but fluency was less stable than in structured business topics.
sessions.nextChallenge: Give a 60-second product comparison and then ask three natural follow-up questions about a colleague’s trip without preparation.

sessions.bestSentence: Then, would you like us to investigate more to decrease the price, or you just accept this price and go further?
sessions.correctedSentence: Would you like us to explore potential cost-saving options, or do you feel comfortable proceeding with the current estimate?
sessions.feedback: You explained the cause of the cost increase and offered the stakeholder a clear decision. Focus on smoother delivery and precise word choice under time pressure.
sessions.nextChallenge: Handle a skeptical stakeholder question about a delay and request a decision.

newExpressions: it feels like a completely different world
sessions.correctedSentence: You should try the seafood, especially abalone, which is famous on Jeju Island.
sessions.feedback: You recommended Jeju Island and Scotland and supported Jeju with scenery and food examples. Build more vivid reasons and retrieve precise vocabulary more quickly.
sessions.nextChallenge: Give a 60-second travel recommendation using a destination, two reasons, and one must-try food.

sessions.topic: Church Orchestra, Pep Talk & Explaining a Delay
newExpressions: get ready to go to church
sessions.bestSentence: I have never given myself a pep talk, but that's a good idea.
sessions.correctedSentence: Although I don't practice during the week, the violin feels different every weekend—some weeks the fingering and bowing feel natural, while other weeks they feel unfamiliar.
sessions.feedback: You sustained an everyday topic and explained how your violin playing changes from week to week. The main communication problems were double negatives, unnecessary connectors, article errors, and unnatural verb combinations. The work-related answer had a clear cause, but it needed a shorter sentence and a concrete recovery plan.
sessions.nextChallenge: Give a 60–90 second everyday story using context, contrast, and reflection, then explain a delay using cause, impact, and recovery.

summary: You described your Sunday preparation and your role in the church orchestra.
You compared how natural or unfamiliar violin fingering and bowing can feel from week to week.
You learned 'pep talk' and practiced explaining a project delay caused by a designer's absence.
learnerSentences: Since it is very early in the morning, so I didn't do nothing.
I took a bath and dried my hair and trimmed, designed my hair.
Although I don't do the play a practice in weekdays, every weekend I feel it is different when it comes to playing the violin.
I have never talked to myself as a pep talk, but that's a good idea.
There was an factor that one of the major factors that the summit of the design has been delayed.

corrections.original: Since it is very early in the morning, so I didn't do nothing.
corrections.selfCorrectionCue: Use either 'since' or 'so,' and remove the double negative.
corrections.natural: Since it's still very early, I haven't done anything yet.
corrections.reason: 'Since' already shows the reason, and 'haven't done anything' is the correct negative form.

corrections.original: I took a bath and dried my hair and trimmed, designed my hair.
corrections.selfCorrectionCue: Which verb means arranging your hair?
corrections.natural: I took a shower, dried my hair, styled it, and chose my clothes.
corrections.reason: Use 'style my hair,' not 'design my hair.' 'Take a shower' is also more natural for an ordinary morning routine.

corrections.original: There was an factor that one of the major factors that the summit of the design has been delayed.
corrections.selfCorrectionCue: Fix the article and state one clear cause.
corrections.natural: One of the main reasons for the delay was that the person in charge of the design was on vacation.
corrections.reason: Use 'a factor,' not 'an factor,' and avoid repeating 'factor' in the same sentence.

targetExpressions.example: Before the performance, I gave myself a quick pep talk and focused on the opening passage.
Some weeks the fingering feels natural, even when I have not practiced much.

targetExpressions.meaning: 여러 원인 가운데 주요 원인 하나를 명확히 제시하다
targetExpressions.example: One of the main reasons for the delay was the temporary shortage of design staff.

lessonNote.finalVersion: I play the violin in my church orchestra every Sunday. What is interesting is that my playing feels different from week to week, even though I rarely practice during the week. Some Sundays, the fingering and bowing feel natural, and I feel confident. On other Sundays, the same movements feel unfamiliar, as if I have not played for a long time. Before the performance, I could give myself a short pep talk: 'Stay calm, listen to the orchestra, and focus on the music rather than worrying about mistakes.'
recallQuestions: How would you describe the difference in your violin playing from week to week?
What could you say to yourself as a short pep talk before performing?
How would you explain a project delay using one clear cause and one recovery action?
answerKey: Although I do not practice during the week, the violin feels different every weekend. Some weeks the fingering and bowing feel natural, while other weeks they feel unfamiliar.
Stay calm, listen carefully, and focus on the music. I can handle the performance one passage at a time.
One of the main reasons for the delay was that the person in charge of the design was on vacation. We have reassigned the remaining work and will provide an updated schedule.
lessonNote.nextChallenge: Speak for 60–90 seconds about an ordinary weekly routine, using one contrast and one reflection without restarting the sentence.

sessions.topic: Project Cost Increase, Delay Explanation & Spontaneous Workplace Speaking
newExpressions: we couldn't meet the original timeline
seek advice from colleagues with similar experience
sessions.bestSentence: I have never been involved in this kind of global work.
sessions.correctedSentence: The client asked why the project cost had increased, and I explained that our local cost estimates were outdated.
sessions.feedback: You communicated the main causes and decision points, but frequent restarts, repeated filler phrases, and long unfinished sentences made the listener work too hard. Your main priority is to state one idea per sentence, finish it, and then move to the next point. You also identified that everyday workplace speaking is harder for you than familiar industry discussions.
sessions.nextChallenge: Give a 60-second spontaneous workplace update using situation, issue, action, and next step without restarting sentences.
sessions.repetitionResult: Improved when repeating short model sentences
sessions.transferResult: Partially successful; concise responses improved, but longer answers remained unstable

summary: You explained a client concern about an increased project budget caused by outdated local cost estimates.
You practiced explaining a delay, presenting a deadline-versus-cost decision, and confirming next steps.
You identified spontaneous daily workplace communication—not familiar technical discussion—as your main speaking difficulty.
learnerSentences: Because the client asked us the reason why the process cost has been increased.
The local data with the cost local data was outdated.
We couldn't catch up earlier.
I have never been involved in this kind of work, global work.
I'm asking the people who are working with similar works to advise me and give me some tips.

corrections.original: The client asked us the reason why the process cost has been increased.
corrections.selfCorrectionCue: Remove the repeated reason structure and use the correct tense.
corrections.natural: The client asked why the project cost had increased.
corrections.reason: 'Asked why' is enough, and past perfect fits because the increase happened before the client asked.

corrections.original: The local data with the cost local data was outdated.
corrections.natural: The local cost estimates were outdated.
corrections.reason: 'Cost estimates' is the precise business term; 'local data with the cost' is unclear.

corrections.selfCorrectionCue: State what deadline or schedule you failed to meet.
corrections.natural: We couldn't meet the original timeline.
corrections.reason: 'Meet the timeline' clearly describes a schedule delay; 'catch up earlier' is vague.

targetExpressions.meaning: 비용 산정 자료가 오래되어 현재 상황을 반영하지 못했다
targetExpressions.example: The project budget increased because the local cost estimates were outdated.
We could not meet the original timeline because the design review took longer than expected.

targetExpressions.expression: seek advice from colleagues with similar experience
targetExpressions.meaning: 비슷한 경험이 있는 동료에게 조언을 구하다
targetExpressions.example: To reduce the risk, I am seeking advice from colleagues with similar global project experience.

lessonNote.finalVersion: The client asked why the project cost had increased. The main reason was that our local cost estimates were outdated, so the original budget no longer reflected current prices. We now need the client to decide whether to protect the deadline by accepting the higher cost or allow more time for us to explore cost-saving options. Because this is my first global project of this type, I am also seeking advice from colleagues with similar experience.
recallQuestions: Why did the project cost increase?
How would you present the deadline-versus-cost decision to the client?
What are you doing to reduce the risk caused by limited global project experience?
answerKey: The project cost increased because the local cost estimates were outdated.
We can protect the deadline by accepting the current estimate, or extend the timeline so we can explore cost-saving options.
I am seeking advice from colleagues who have handled similar global projects.
lessonNote.nextChallenge: Answer five unexpected workplace questions using one complete idea per sentence, then deliver a 60-second structured update without restarting.

sessions.sessionManagementNote: Use the full planned 20–25 minutes. Do not end early; continue with additional questions or exercises while time remains, and confirm whether the learner wants to continue before issuing the final report.

sessions.topic: Date Confusion, Back-and-Forth, Weather Delay & Direct Workplace Feedback
newExpressions: The delay was due to two weeks of heavy rain.
Decisions are being made without full team input.
sessions.bestSentence: The biggest risk in our project is you.
sessions.correctedSentence: The main risk is that decisions are being made without enough team input, which may cause us to overlook important local conditions.
sessions.feedback: You handled an unexpected everyday topic with humor and explained a weather-related project delay using cause, impact, and compliance risk. Your confidence was strong when expressing disagreement, but grammar accuracy and sentence control dropped as your answer became more emotional and complex. Keep the direct message, but organize it as observation, impact, evidence, and request.
sessions.nextChallenge: Give a 60-second direct but professional disagreement using observation, impact, evidence, and a specific request without restarting sentences.
sessions.repetitionResult: Accurately repeated the concise weather-delay model
sessions.transferResult: Strong directness, but the professional structure was only partially transferred

summary: You described the humorous date confusion from August 3 versus August 5 and learned the phrase 'back-and-forth.'
You explained a two-week rain delay and the need to comply with project regulations to avoid penalties.
You practiced criticizing centralized decision-making and converting personal criticism into a persuasive professional risk statement.
learnerSentences: Actually, your word has a dilemma.
There have been raining, so which make the project delayed.
The biggest risk in our project is you.
You make all decisions by yourself, and you don't hear our opinions.
Your way of talking is not effective to persuade our company to make our project success.

corrections.original: Actually, your word has a dilemma.
corrections.selfCorrectionCue: Describe a mismatch between two statements, not a moral dilemma.
corrections.natural: Your two statements contradict each other.
corrections.reason: A dilemma is a difficult choice between options. Here, 'contradict' or 'do not match' expresses the meaning accurately.

corrections.original: There have been raining, so which make the project delayed.
corrections.selfCorrectionCue: Use the weather subject 'it' and a clear cause-result structure.
corrections.natural: It rained heavily for two weeks, which delayed the project.
corrections.reason: Use 'it rained' for weather and 'which delayed' to describe the result.

corrections.original: Your way of talking is not effective to persuade our company to make our project success.
corrections.natural: Your communication style is not effective in persuading the company or helping the project succeed.
corrections.reason: The natural patterns are 'effective in doing something' and 'help the project succeed.'

targetExpressions.meaning: 두 사람이 여러 차례 주고받는 대화나 논쟁
targetExpressions.example: After a long back-and-forth, we finally clarified the correct date.
The delay was due to two weeks of heavy rain.
The main risk is that key decisions are being made without full team input.

lessonNote.finalVersion: The main risk is that key decisions are being made without enough team input. Our team has investigated the local conditions and identified several factors that could significantly affect the schedule. If those findings are not considered, the project may face avoidable delays and costs. I would like us to review the evidence together before making the final decision.
recallQuestions: What does 'back-and-forth' mean, and how would you use it to describe today's date confusion?
How would you explain the weather delay in two concise sentences?
How would you criticize centralized decision-making directly but professionally?
answerKey: A back-and-forth is a repeated exchange between two sides. We had a funny back-and-forth because the date was repeatedly stated as August 3 even though it was August 5.
The delay was due to two weeks of heavy rain. We will resume work as soon as conditions allow while following all safety and project regulations.
The main risk is that decisions are being made without enough team input. I would like us to review the team's local evidence before finalizing the decision.
lessonNote.nextChallenge: Deliver a direct disagreement in four steps: observation, impact, evidence, and request.

sessions.topic: Condensed Reporting Work, Scope Clarification & Prioritization
newExpressions: review five years of work in a short time
ask the PIC for the exact scope and priorities
sessions.bestSentence: Reviewing five years of work in a short time is annoying.
sessions.correctedSentence: Next time, I'll ask the PIC for the exact scope and priorities first to streamline the work.
sessions.feedback: You explained why reviewing several years of condensed work was frustrating and identified a practical prevention strategy: clarify scope and priorities before starting. Fluency improved when you shortened the message, but longer answers still showed restarts, incomplete structures, and unclear preposition choices. Keep using one complete idea per sentence and clarify purpose before detail.
sessions.nextChallenge: Give a 60-second explanation of an overloaded task using problem, cause, clarification request, and expected benefit without restarting sentences.
sessions.selfCorrection: Successful on short corrections such as 'It was annoying / It was bothering me,' but longer planning sentences still required reformulation.
sessions.repetitionResult: Successful when repeating concise target phrases such as 'ask for the exact scope and priorities first.'
sessions.transferResult: Partial: the learner added a collaborative softener and purpose, but sentence structure became unstable again in the longer version.

summary: You described the frustration of reviewing about five years of team work in a short period.
You practiced compressing a long explanation into one clear sentence and self-corrected 'annoying' versus 'bothering me.'
You developed a prevention strategy: ask the PIC for the exact scope and priorities first so the work can be streamlined.
learnerSentences: The time consuming... I need screen lots of documents and content.
If that kind of work comes again, I mean occur again...
The purpose is the first priority before...
Make sure understanding makes it work.
I think I will ask for the PIC... exact scope and priorities first.

corrections.original: The time consuming... I need screen lots of documents and content.
corrections.selfCorrectionCue: Make 'time-consuming' an adjective and use a natural verb for documents.
corrections.natural: It was time-consuming because I had to review a lot of documents and content.
corrections.reason: Use 'time-consuming' after 'be,' and 'review/go through documents' is more natural than 'screen' here.

corrections.original: If that kind of work comes again, I mean occur again...
corrections.selfCorrectionCue: Use a natural phrasal verb for a task appearing again.
corrections.natural: If that kind of task comes up again, I'll clarify the scope first.
corrections.reason: For tasks or requests, 'come up again' sounds natural; 'work occurs' is too formal and awkward in this context.

corrections.original: I think I will ask for the PIC... exact scope and priorities first.
corrections.selfCorrectionCue: Who are you asking, and what are you asking for?
corrections.natural: I think I'll ask the PIC for the exact scope and priorities first.
corrections.reason: The pattern is 'ask someone for something,' so 'ask the PIC for the scope' gives the roles clearly.

targetExpressions.example: If a similar reporting task comes up again, I'll clarify the requirements first.

targetExpressions.expression: ask someone for the exact scope and priorities
targetExpressions.example: Before I start, I'll ask the PIC for the exact scope and priorities.

targetExpressions.meaning: 불필요한 단계를 줄여 일을 더 효율적으로 만들다
targetExpressions.example: Clear priorities will help us streamline the work and avoid reviewing unnecessary documents.

lessonNote.finalVersion: Today I had to review several years of our team's work in a very short time, so the task was quite time-consuming. I had to go through a large number of documents, and the required scope was not completely clear at first. If a similar task comes up again, I'll ask the PIC for the exact scope and priorities before I start. That should help me focus only on the necessary information, streamline the work, and avoid wasting time on material that is not needed.
recallQuestions: Why was today's reporting task frustrating and time-consuming?
What will you ask the PIC before starting a similar task next time?
How will clarifying the scope and priorities help your work?
answerKey: It was time-consuming because I had to review several years of work and a large number of documents in a short period.
I'll ask the PIC for the exact scope and priorities first.
It will help me focus on the necessary information and streamline the work.
lessonNote.nextChallenge: Explain an overloaded task for 60 seconds using problem, cause, clarification request, and benefit without restarting.
